req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT change the default 302; (4) verify the Location header is set to the exact url supplied; (5) test missing status_code falls back to 302; (6) test non-redirect status_code values are rejected. This covers EP, BVA, DT, NEG heuristics and catches operator-flip mutations (>= vs >, < vs <=), constant mutations (302->303, 300->301, 400->399), and boolean/branch mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_status_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_status_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_status_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url
expected: Location header is exactly https://target.example.org/path?q=1 (verbatim, not modified)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: Location header must equal the exact url parameter supplied
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url():
    target = 'https://target.example.org/path?q=1'
    r = client.get(
        '/redirect-to?url=' + target + '&status_code=307',
        follow_redirects=False
    )
    assert r.status_code == 307
    assert r.headers['Location'] == target

test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact
actions: Iterate over [301,302,303,307,308] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code matches the requested code exactly
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: all five required status codes must be honoured; catches constant-swap mutations
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, f'Expected {code}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_non_redirect_codes_all_yield_302
actions: Iterate over [100,200,400,404,500] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code is exactly 302 (default preserved for all non-3xx values)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: NEG — non-redirect codes must all be ignored; catches missing-branch mutations
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_non_redirect_codes_all_yield_302():
    for code in [100, 200, 400, 404, 500]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'code={code}: expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_non_redirect_codes_all_yield_302()
